user.title: LSC Tuya Doorbell Setup
user.description: Choose how to add your doorbell.

pick_device.title: Select Device
pick_device.description: Found {count} device(s) you can still add ({skipped} already configured). Pick your doorbell, or configure one manually.

data_description.protocol_version: If you are unsure, leave this at 3.3 — the other versions are tried automatically when it does not work.

credentials.title: Device Credentials

data_description.protocol_version: What the device speaks over TCP. Leave it alone if you are unsure.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-enter Local Key
reauth_confirm.description:
Tuya changed the local key of {name} ({device_id} at {host}), so the doorbell no longer accepts the stored one. This happens when a device is re-paired in the Tuya or Smart Life app.

Look up the new local key and enter it here. Your entities and automations stay exactly as they are.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Device
reconfigure.description: Change the connection details for {device_id}. The new settings are tested before they are saved, and your entities keep their IDs.

progress.discovering: Listening for Tuya broadcasts on the local network. Devices announce themselves every few seconds, so this takes up to 10 seconds.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the device. Check the IP address and port, and that the doorbell is powered on and on the same network.
error.heartbeat_failed: The device accepted the connection but never answered. This usually means the local key is wrong for this device.
error.invalid_local_key_length: A local key is exactly 16 characters.
error.invalid_local_key: The device rejected this local key. Look it up again in the Tuya IoT developer portal — Tuya changes it whenever a device is re-paired.
error.unsupported_protocol_version: The device speaks a Tuya protocol version this integration does not support (only 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 are supported). Devices on 3.1 or 3.2 need a firmware update, or have to be used through the Tuya cloud integration.
error.decryption_failed: The device's reply could not be decrypted. That means either the local key or the protocol version is wrong.
error.protocol_error: The device sent something this integration could not read. Check the logs — the protocol layer records exactly which frame failed.
error.timeout: The device did not answer in time. It may be asleep, busy streaming, or on a poor Wi-Fi connection.
error.discovery_failed: Discovery could not run. Check the logs, and add the doorbell manually with its IP address and device ID.
error.unknown: An unexpected error occurred. Check the logs for details.

abort.reauth_successful: The new local key works — the doorbell is connected again.
abort.reconfigure_successful: The new settings work and have been saved.
abort.entry_not_found: That configuration entry no longer exists.

init.title: LSC Tuya Doorbell Options
init.description:
Choose what you want to configure. Each screen saves when you submit it and brings you back here, so you can do several things in a row; use 'Close' when you are done.

Debugging timing? Turn on 'Debug: realtime datapoint events' below. While it is on, every datapoint the doorbell reports is mirrored to the event bus as `lsc_tuya_doorbell_debug_dp` the moment it arrives, with a monotonic timestamp -- watch it live under Developer Tools → Events to see exactly when a button press lands.

menu_options.live_capture: Live capture (find button and motion datapoints)

menu_option_descriptions.connection: IP address, port and Tuya protocol version.
menu_option_descriptions.camera_settings: Where the video comes from, and what is done with it.
menu_option_descriptions.snapshot_settings: How a picture is produced when the doorbell fires.
menu_option_descriptions.dp_list: Rename, retype or delete the datapoints this device has.
menu_option_descriptions.dp_scan_mode: Ask the device which datapoints it will answer for.
menu_option_descriptions.live_capture: Watch what the device reports while you press the doorbell. The only way to find an event datapoint.
menu_option_descriptions.capture_review: Pick datapoints out of the last live capture.
menu_option_descriptions.assign_roles: Say which datapoint is the button, the motion sensor and the record switch.
menu_option_descriptions.firmware_generation: Which datapoint-name table applies to this device.
menu_option_descriptions.debug_settings: Mirror every datapoint to the event bus as it arrives, for live timing in Developer Tools → Events. Off by default.
menu_option_descriptions.finish: Close this dialog. Everything you submitted is already saved.

It gets an event entity alongside its normal one, and the live capture marks likely candidates with ⟳. It cannot be worked out automatically: a volume slider moved twice looks the same from here.

camera_settings.title: Camera Settings
camera_settings.description:
Where the video comes from decides which settings mean anything, so that question comes first and the next screen asks only what applies.

These cameras get confused by several simultaneous RTSP sessions. Measured on a real doorbell: a snapshot takes 5.86 s on its own, and 15.94 s when a second grab is already holding a session open. Home Assistant's stream, a snapshot, HomeKit and a detection service add up to four connections fast. A restreamer such as go2rtc or Frigate keeps one connection to the doorbell and fans it out — that is the whole reason the option exists.

The two settings below apply either way.

**Submit opens the settings for the source you picked.**

data.video_source: Where does the video come from?
data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing on this screen is saved)

data_description.video_source: Pre-selected from what is already configured: a stream URL override means a restreamer is in front of the camera.
data_description.snapshot_path: Where taken pictures are written. Home Assistant serves the www folder of your configuration as /local, so the default ends up at /local/doorbell/... and that URL is what the events carry. Only the ten most recent files per device are kept.
data_description.force_onvif: Some Tuya devices turn ONVIF — and with it the RTSP stream — off by themselves, for instance after a reboot. This pushes it back on. It only does anything when a datapoint holds the 'ONVIF switch' role, which you set under 'Assign roles to datapoints'. Right now {onvif_role}.

snapshot_settings.title: Snapshot Settings
snapshot_settings.description:
How a picture is produced when the doorbell fires. The four modes read different settings, so the mode comes first and the next screen asks only what this mode uses.

Measured on a real doorbell:
- ffmpeg grab straight from the camera: 5.86 s
- the same grab with a second one already running: 15.94 s
- go2rtc still image, source already warm: 1.82 – 3.09 s
- a continuous ffmpeg writing a rolling JPEG: 1.00 s, flat

The delay is not the network. The keyframe is decoded after about a second and ffmpeg then spends five to six more working out what the stream contains; no flag shortens that, so anything that starts a process per press pays it every time.

**Submit opens the settings this mode uses.**

data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing on this screen is saved)

data_description.snapshot_mode: 'Off' takes no pictures at all. 'On demand' starts one ffmpeg per press: slow, but it needs nothing and works anywhere, which is why it is the default. 'Warm' keeps one ffmpeg running so a still is always about a second old. 'Buffer' additionally keeps the last minute of video on tmpfs and is the only mode that can look back in time — which matters, because the device reports a press three to five seconds after it happened. 'Clip' records like buffer but, instead of a still, saves the whole buffer as a short video when the doorbell fires — handy on a slow host, or when you want the moments around the press.

dp_scan_mode.title: Scan for Datapoints
dp_scan_mode.description:
The scan asks the device for every datapoint it will answer for (DP 1-255). This can take up to 2 minutes.

Nothing is saved until you have picked what to keep. Datapoints that only fire on an event — the doorbell button, motion — cannot be found this way; use live capture for those.

You can safely close this dialog while the scan runs and come back for the results.

data.clear_existing: Replace all existing datapoints with the scan results
data.force_rescan: Run a new scan (discard the previous results)
data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing on this screen is saved)

dp_scan_failed.title: Scan Failed
dp_scan_failed.description: The datapoint scan did not complete. Try again, or go back to the options menu.

dp_scan_results.title: Scan Results
dp_scan_results.description:
Found {count} datapoint(s). Tick the ones to add, or to refresh with what this scan learned about them.

Datapoints already in the profile stay whether you tick them or not — unticking one does not remove it. To remove a datapoint, use **Manage datapoints** in the options menu.

data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing on this screen is saved)

live_capture.title: Live Capture
live_capture.description: Recording what the device reports needs a live connection to it. Fix the connection first, then start the capture again.

data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing on this screen is saved)

capture_review.title: Capture Results
capture_review.description:
The capture saw {count} datapoint(s). Pick the ones to keep; ⟳ marks the ones that behave like events.

{detail}

data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing on this screen is saved)

assign_roles.title: Assign Roles
assign_roles.description:
A datapoint without a role is just a sensor: the integration reads roles, not numbers, so this is where the doorbell button becomes the doorbell button.

Only the doorbell button really matters. Motion is optional, and the ONVIF switch is only needed if you use 'Force ONVIF on' — it is the switch that gets turned back on when the device turns it off by itself, which also brings the RTSP stream back.

Datapoints marked 'already configured' were found earlier; leaving a role pointed at one keeps it as it was.

data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing on this screen is saved)

firmware_generation.title: Datapoint names

data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing on this screen is saved)

camera_direct.title: Camera: Direct Connection
camera_direct.description:
The stream URL is built from the device's IP address ({host}), the port and the path below, and everything that wants video opens its own session to the doorbell.

Submitting this screen clears any stream URL override: the two describe different setups and only one of them can win.

data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing from these two screens is saved)

camera_restream.title: Camera: Through a Restreamer
camera_restream.description:
One connection to the doorbell, fanned out to everything else. Point both fields at the restreamer, not at the camera — in 2.x the snapshot code rebuilt its own URL from host, port and path, which is how a fourth session ended up on the camera even with an override set.

The RTSP port and path are not used while this is in place.

data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing from these two screens is saved)

data_description.stream_url_override: The restreamer's RTSP URL, for example rtsp://192.168.1.10:8554/doorbell.

snapshot_options.title: Snapshot Mode Settings
snapshot_options.description: Settings for the {mode} snapshot mode. Only what this mode actually reads is shown.{buffer_note}{trigger_hint}

data.snapshot_trigger_dps: Take a snapshot when these datapoints fire
data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing from these two screens is saved)

data_description.snapshot_trigger_dps: Only datapoints this device actually reports are listed. Run a scan or a live capture to fill this list.
data_description.snapshot_buffer_path: Put it on tmpfs (/dev/shm) so the segments never touch persistent storage; see above for the size it needs.
data_description.snapshot_buffer_seconds: How much video is kept. Longer means more memory. In the 'clip' mode this is also the length of the saved clip.
data_description.snapshot_delay_ms: The doorbell reports a press seconds after it happened, so a picture of 'now' shows the visitor already walking away. This takes the picture that many milliseconds earlier. Start around 3000 ms and adjust.
data_description.still_image_url_override: Where to fetch a single picture, if something on your network can hand one over — go2rtc's /api/frame.jpeg, Frigate's latest.jpg, or a camera that serves stills over HTTP. When this is set it is always tried first, in every mode, because it costs one request. Leave it empty to take pictures from the video stream instead.
data_description.snapshot_source_url: Leave empty to record from whatever the camera streams from. Set it when the two should differ — if something on your network already restreams this doorbell for other reasons, point this at that instead of standing up a second one. It also works the other way round: record straight from the doorbell while the camera goes through a restreamer.

debug_settings.title: Debug: realtime datapoint events
debug_settings.description:
When on, every datapoint the doorbell reports is fired on the Home Assistant event bus as `{debug_event}` the instant it arrives, carrying the datapoint number, its value, the previous value, and a monotonic timestamp taken at arrival.

Subscribe to `{debug_event}` under Developer Tools → Events to watch the doorbell in real time -- this is how you measure the delay between a button press and anything reacting to it. It is chatty, so leave it off for normal use.

data.debug_events: Fire a realtime event for every datapoint
data.back: Back to the options menu (nothing on this screen is saved)

error.unsupported_protocol_version: The device speaks a Tuya protocol version this integration does not support (only 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5 are supported).
error.decryption_failed: The device's reply could not be decrypted. That means either the local key or the protocol version is wrong.

options.on_demand: On demand — fetch a picture when the doorbell fires (default)
options.warm: Warm — a rolling still kept ready, about 1.0 s
options.buffer: Buffer — recent video kept on tmpfs, the only mode that can look back
options.clip: Clip — save a video of the whole buffer when the doorbell fires

options.direct: Directly from the camera — you give the host, port and path
options.restream: From a restreamer (go2rtc, Frigate) — you give the stream URL

no_doorbell_role.title: No doorbell button datapoint on {device_name}
no_doorbell_role.description:
Home Assistant does not know which datapoint on {device_name} (`{device_id}`) reports a button press, so pressing the doorbell will not trigger anything.

Datapoint numbers differ between models and firmware versions, so they cannot be assumed. Open the integration options and run **Live capture**, then press the doorbell while it listens. Assign the datapoint that appears to the doorbell button role.
